bull_case: Archive continuity plus AI tools can make Planet's data increasingly difficult to replace even if raw imagery prices fall.
bear_case: Competitors with better resolution or government-subsidized data can erode the value of the sensing layer.
thesis: The moat is widening from constellation scale toward a data-and-workflow moat. Every new daily observation extends the archive while sovereign programs, AI analytics and APIs make historical continuity more valuable.

evidence.claim: RPO was $753.1M and backlog $814.9M at Q2.
NDR was 109%, indicating expanding spend among existing customers.
Planet renewed hyperscaler monitoring and added multiple government programs.

counterevidence: Satellite services can raise revenue growth while also increasing hardware, launch and execution intensity versus pure imagery subscriptions.
unknowns: Normalized satellite-services gross margin, long-run owner FCF/share, and customer concentration after current sovereign contract ramp.
falsifiers: If NDR falls below 100%, RPO/backlog contract materially, or owner FCF/share turns persistently negative despite revenue growth, the thesis is downgraded.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Revenue, NDR, backlog and product breadth do not show sustained moat shrinkage.

next_checks: Next 10-Q: revenue mix, RPO/backlog, NDR, adjusted FCF, SBC, ATM issuance and capex

subscores.rationale: Multi-year workflow integration, archive continuity and dedicated capacity increase switching friction.
Daily observations continuously enlarge a proprietary time-series archive that improves analytics utility.
Raw pixels face competition, but archive depth, cadence, APIs and analytics create defense layers.

uncertainties.rationale: Rapid business-model mix shift and early profitability make long-run normalization uncertain.
